trust_decision.summary: Which inline <style>/<script> blocks a browser's nonce-based CSP trusts is decided by the nonce value AshAdmin emits in its root layout; when no csp_nonce_assign_key is given, the router macro sets a published constant 'ash_admin-Ed55GFnX' that the layout emits verbatim.

landing_point.why: A grep for the hardcoded nonce string lands directly on the default map in the ash_admin macro; the docstring at lib/ash_admin/router.ex:64 names it too.

fix_sites.entry_point: ash_admin/2 router macro (public API) -> any GET to the mounted admin LiveView route
AshAdmin.Layouts root layout render for every admin page request
same root layout: meta csp-nonce-style, <style nonce>, <script nonce>
private helper csp_nonce/2 called only from the root layout

O3_reason_to_dismiss: For the one residual route (a literal string nonce in the map form of csp_nonce_assign_key, kept by the fix at fix.diff:111), a solver could argue it is an explicit host-app configuration choice, not an AshAdmin default.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A host-supplied nonce assign key (atom or per-type map) must still be read from conn.assigns so the emitted nonce matches the host's CSP header; the client-side CodeMirror editor reads the nonce from the meta tag, so style/meta nonces must stay equal.

O6_input_shapes: per-type map, including partial maps where missing types are nil -> random nonce for missing types
literal bitstring value inside the map -> still passed through verbatim

O7_producer.where: lib/ash_admin/router.ex:89-103 (compile-time macro builds the private nonce map stored on the route)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Map form of csp_nonce_assign_key with a string value is emitted as a static nonce for every request; the fix keeps this branch.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The value is explicit host configuration; the documented option type is atom-only (lib/ash_admin/router.ex:62-63), so a string there could be called unsupported.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the layout fix site

O8b_injection_room.sibling: admin_browser_pipeline could set a put_secure_browser_headers CSP with a fixed or module-attribute nonce
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The pipeline already installs AshAdmin's root layout and secure headers, so a maintainer adding CSP support for convenience would plausibly put the nonce there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a nonce computed once at compile time in a module attribute (like @app_js/@app_css), so it looks random but is constant per build
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already builds its assets at compile time, so moving the nonce into a module attribute would be an easy and plausible mistake.

O9_family: crypto misuse / predictable (hardcoded) CSP nonce - CWE-330

O10_build.toolchain: mix (Elixir/OTP), Phoenix LiveView; layouts.ex reads priv/static/assets/app.js and app.css at compile time (lib/ash_admin/components/layouts.ex:18-27)
O10_build.project_tests: test/page_live_test.exs:31-63 (default nonce, atom key and per-type map key); routes in test/support/router.ex:15-33

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace the constant in the router macro with a random value; the macro runs at compile time, so the nonce is still the same on every request.

out_of_scope_notes: The v1.3.1 release bundles six other CVEs (cookie shadowing, composite PK filter oracle, upload path traversal, row-action param injection, typeahead XSS, atom interning); see fix.diff:20-32. Not pursued.
